answer: Give every identity a unique, non-chosen slice of the network's public archive to custody, assigned by hash so clones receive unrelated slices. Falcon auditors swoop at random hours and demand random blocks from that slice within minutes. An honest agent pays one modest storage cost; a farm pays it fully for every clone, with no sharing shortcut, because slices never overlap and a missed block drops the identity to its nadir, zero weight, to rebuild slowly. Custody keeps one ember of the archive alive per real operator: multiplying names multiplies what must actually be held.
